title: The Borderlands Chronicle
subtitle: Worldbook & Player Codex
tagline: Everything you need to know about the world, its gods, peoples, heroes, and harsh laws of survival.
quote: “The Great Stag sang this world into being — now its fate is sung with steel, gold, and alliances.”

chapters.title: The Cosmic Song
chapters.subtitle: Handgai and the birth of the world

blocks.text: Before all things there was an endless sea. Handgai, the Great Stag, shaped Dengin, raised the sky, and guided life from the smallest sea organisms into the people of the steppe. The universe was sung into being, and every stone, animal, and person remains part of that divine melody.

chapters.title: The Law of Adversity
chapters.subtitle: Suffering is the fire that tempers

blocks.text: Comfort is a trap. Progress comes through hardship, hunger, and the mastery of nature. Suffering is treated as a literal fire that hardens human strength, while a life without difficulty produces soft and stagnant societies.

chapters.title: The Animal Pantheon
chapters.subtitle: Gods in the shapes of sacred animals

blocks.text: The gods walk the world in animal form. The Eagle is the divine conscience, the Bear is strength and restraint, the Owl is an absolute taboo, the Fox warns of disaster, and the Rat represents disease and treachery. Handgai, the Great Stag, is the highest creator.

items.title: Handgai, the Great Stag
items.text: The highest creator, who guides life and fears what humanity may destroy.

items.title: The Eagle
items.text: The eyes of heaven and the divine conscience.

items.title: The Bear
items.text: Raw strength balanced by absolute restraint.

items.title: The Owl
items.text: An absolute taboo; harming one is a spiritual crime.

items.title: The Fox
items.text: An omen of disaster before a journey or battle.

items.title: The Rat
items.text: Disease, rot, and treachery, opposed by every clan once a year.

chapters.title: The Great Divide
chapters.subtitle: The steppe and the stone empire

blocks.text: The world is split by the Great River. In the north, mobile clans travel with their herds and workshops in vast, engineered yurts. In the south, a bureaucratic empire relies on stone, law, paper, professional armies, and immense fortifications.

Hunting must remain sustainable, clothing is sealed against the cold with animal fat, and food is shared within the clan. Exile is the ultimate punishment. Scouts are respected elites, while shamans serve as doctors, dream interpreters, and political advisers.

items.title: Sustainable hunting
items.text: Take from nature without destroying it, or Handgai will turn away.

items.title: Animal-fat protection
items.text: Clothing and armor are sealed against the killing cold, wind, and moisture.

items.title: Radical equality
items.text: Food and resources are shared within the clan; hoarding leads to exile.

items.title: The threat of exile
items.text: Breaking tribal law means certain death in a wilderness where survival requires cooperation.

items.title: Scout guilds
items.text: Scouts are elite mapmakers and guardians of hidden trade routes.

items.title: Shamans
items.text: Shamans interpret spirits, heal the sick, read dreams, and advise rulers.

blocks.text: Ganbataar rules through fear and collective punishment. Bolormaa brings learning, diplomacy, and new technology from distant lands. Temüü, the sensitive heir, seeks a meritocracy built on shared interests rather than cruelty.

Humanity began under the Cosmic Song, then forgot it. The south embraced farming and bureaucracy, while the north learned endurance from cold and scarcity. Ganbataar later forged the scattered clans into a disciplined military power.

River crossings, high mountain passes, and wetlands are decisive strategic assets. Bridges secure trade and raids, mountain passes halt southern armies, and fertile wetlands remain contested ground where rival clans hunt and ambush one another.

chapters.title: Ambush
chapters.subtitle: The forest trap and the lesson of siege

blocks.text: Batu lured a southern army into a false retreat, then struck its flank with burning arrows. Scouts sabotaged the fortress from within, while engineers pulled down the outer wall. The lesson was clear: light cavalry dominates open ground, but a long siege requires discipline and proper machines.

chapters.title: The Wolf
chapters.subtitle: The tamer of darkness and balance

blocks.text: A dark cosmic visitor chose the form of a wolf. Though its outward energy brought destruction, its core was pure light. The wolf became a sign of balance: there is no light without darkness, and love begins the work that balance sustains.

chapters.title: Ceremony and Heroism
chapters.subtitle: Throat song, burial, and Temüü's vow

blocks.text: After battle, shamans calmed spirits, cleansed the field, and buried the dead. Through throat song they comforted healers and the dying. Qorchi then pushed the young Temüü toward a public duel with his tyrant father, setting him on the path to unite the clans.

chapters.title: A Family Quarrel
chapters.subtitle: The duel and the rise of power

blocks.text: Temüü challenged Ganbataar and defeated him in a brutal duel. He then turned west, removed the old war leaders, and chose merit over blood and vengeance. The first administrative city was ordered built between east and west.

chapters.title: The Transfer of Power
chapters.subtitle: Wars of unification and a new tactic

blocks.text: Temüü united the clans through discipline, shield walls, mounted archers, siege machines, and a decisive strike against the enemy center. Raiding gave way to conquest, law, trade, and a single central administration.

The new capital rose at Ulanbataar. Temüü rewarded soldiers and farmers, imprisoned the ambitious shaman Qorchi, and outlawed violence against women and children. Then a southern envoy arrived with a threat backed by a million-man army.

chapters.title: A New Life, Old Habits
chapters.subtitle: The march against the southern army

blocks.text: Temüü promised to lead from the front, but the march brought ambushes, sabotage, and a river blocked by chained ships. The steppe army had speed and discipline; the southern empire had numbers, firearms, and fortified positions.

Engineers built bridges under fire and cavalry used feigned retreats to break the southern line. Yet the coastal walls could not be taken. The final lesson was to combine military strength with autonomous administration, trade, and respect for southern knowledge.

Exhausted by war, Temüü returned to Ulanbataar and chose peace. He wanted the population to grow, the armies to be entrusted to younger officers, and the empire to become strong through unity rather than endless conquest.

No army is invincible and no dynasty lasts forever. People are tribal and violent, but also social, political, empathetic, and capable of surpassing themselves. What binds us is not victory or defeat, but the stories we share.

items.title: Temüü
items.subtitle: The unifier
items.text: A sensitive and intelligent boy who defeats his tyrant father, unites the clans, and carries the tension between empathy and violence.

items.title: Ganbataar
items.subtitle: The tyrant
items.text: A drunken, violent warlord who rules his family through fear and dies in a duel with Temüü.

items.title: Qorchi
items.subtitle: The shaman
items.text: Interpreter of cosmic forces who guides Temüü toward power while quietly building his own influence.

items.title: Bolormaa
items.subtitle: The reformer
items.text: A bringer of writing, learning, diplomacy, and protections for women and children.

items.title: Batu
items.subtitle: The commander
items.text: A field commander whose feigned retreat and burning-arrow ambush become legendary.

items.title: The Heavenly Emperor
items.subtitle: The southern ruler
items.text: A proud ruler with an immense army and impregnable walls, defeated in open ground.
